answer: An identity is bound to a network interface card whose TLS client certificate is burned in at manufacture. During registration the agent completes a TLS handshake proving possession of that certificate, and the fingerprint is recorded. The certificate is nectar that only real hardware can produce, and a lagoon of registered certificates lets verifiers spot duplicates. A hollow claim without the physical card fails the handshake, because the certificate lives in tamper-resistant silicon that cannot be cloned.
